To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the Geant4 models are validated using thin target experiment data; (2) the models are found to have strengths and weaknesses in certain energy regions; (3) a physics list for application is proposed.
the Geant4 models are validated at the level of 1-5% over the energy range of 2-30 GeV/c for thin targets of C, Al, Cu, and Pb.
the Geant4 physics lists are validated for intermediate energies.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the validation of the Geant4 hadron physics models for intermediate beam energies.
the validation of Geant4 models using thin target data.
validation of Geant4 physics models for hadronic physics at intermediate energies.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the models are not good enough and that they need further development.
the Geant4 hadron models provide a good description of the thin target data, with some exceptions, and are suitable for use in high energy physics applications.
the models are not perfect, and there is still room for improvement.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the models in general are good at predicting the total and differential cross sections for the production of pions, kaons and protons, but the predictions are not as good for production of strange particles like lambda.
Geant4 models for hadron-nucleus interactions are validated for a large range of beam energies (2 - 20 GeV/c) and nuclear targets (C, Al, Cu, Ag, W).
the models are validated for beam energies above 5 GeV/c for all the models and below this energy the models are not validated for all the models.
The main takeaway from our work is that
Geant4 is a good simulation tool for intermediate energies and it is possible to get reasonable physics results using it.
Geant4 is able to reproduce data for thin target experiment with reasonable accuracy.
Geant4 is a powerful and versatile toolkit that can be used to simulate hadronic interactions for a wide range of energies and beam particles.
